trecho.0: opeus: Evgene Bavcar, Mercedes Replinger, Adolfo Montejo Navas, Roland Campos, Angélica Madeira, Bené Fonteles and Marília Panitz produced an important body of reflections that accompany this compilation of records that survived time. It is possible, in this way, to traverse here twenty years of history through the projects and the installations: “Experiência Tumulto (1985)”, “Cubo Cruz Lápide (1985)”, “O Profeta e a Jaguatirica (1985-86)”, “DO AKD-MICO AO POLE-MICO (1986)”, “Mognus Dei (1990)”, “O Sol de Goethe (1999)”, “São João Beuys (1990)”, “Ser ou não Ser, Ao Gullar (1993)”, “Pega Manet/De Onde Vem A Escuridão (1986)”, “TV Anal (1999)”, “Hermógenes (1999)”, “Obranome (2003)” and “Cultura X Natureza = Barbárie (1998/2005)” Marília Panitz, in her text “Ao que importa, uma resposta”, proposes an itinerary for reading Barja’s works, starting from the concept of equation, so dear to the artist. In the “enigmas of visual equations” of Barja’s commentary-constructions, the author highlights the condensation of meanings that has humor as its tool. trecho.1: of another anonymous one who is later discovered to be Lygia Clark? ...A poetic proposal that accounts for the unexpectedness of the fact (which is real). Another tombstone, perhaps. A FIKE that unravels the threads of the proposal of modernity taken to the extreme (its end). The yellow, blue and red ribbons, a fitting homage to one who defied these extremes and eliminated the frontiers between art and the (other) things of the world (with its many other threads unraveled in various works). What to leave to the world, Mondrian? Yellow, blue and red ribbons that appear recurrently as a metaphor for a thought about (of) painting, as in De onde vem a escuridão or in “ Pega Manet ”[4]. In the first work, they are links between the parts that do not necessarily converse among themselves, they are the (impossible) support of the concrete swing/bar NEO and they are the water of the fountain that issues from the mouth of the baroque lion onto the black screen from which the head projects itself... Or a possible path between the inscription in expressive excess and the illusion of the economy of the minimum, pure color and orthogonal form (a path traveled by the same strips of the work for Lygia).
